prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Yes We Can — win the best for Scotland. The SNP’s 1997 manifesto sets out a confident, costed route to independence so Scotland can put its wealth to work for jobs, fairness and modern public services — not Westminster priorities.

Scotland’s choice is clear. Scotland is a wealthy nation that has paid more into the UK than it has received. With independence, Scotland would be among the world’s richer small states, automatically in the EU, with open borders to England, secure pensions and investments, and a modern non‑nuclear defence. All who live here keep full residence rights; citizenship rests on birth or residency.

How we gain independence. A majority of SNP MPs will trigger negotiations with the UK and the EU, followed by a simple confirmatory referendum within 6–12 months. On approval, independence is declared and fresh elections held.

A democracy for all. An independent Scotland will have a written constitution and Bill of Rights guaranteeing civil and social rights (free healthcare, education, fair work and a minimum wage), PR elections, votes from 16, entrenched local government, and a reformed constitutional monarchy with transparent duties and costs.

Prosperity with fairness. The SNP targets full employment and 100,000 new jobs through:
- Competitive business taxes: cut main corporation tax to 30p and small companies to 18p; abolish Class IV NICs; fair, banded business rates.
- Smart investment: R&D boosts, export support, skills foundation, doubled tourism marketing, defence diversification.
- Modern infrastructure: Railtrack in public ownership in Scotland; rail electrification; integrated buses; no new tolls (Skye tolls ended); better ferries; fairer air duty for remote areas; world‑class telecoms and support for teleworking.

Fair personal taxation. Introduce a 15p starter rate; widen the basic rate band; remove the NICs ceiling for high earners; cut VAT on domestic fuel to 5%. Most workers pay less; those best‑paid contribute slightly more.

Social justice, health and safety. Raise child benefit; restore support for 16–17‑year‑olds; increase pensions, add a Cold Climate Allowance, end means‑testing for residential care. Rebuild a real National Health Service: scrap the internal market, reintegrate dentistry, expand prevention (ban tobacco ads, raise tobacco duty), and audit quality. Tackle crime with “zero tolerance” of vandalism, better courts and alternatives to prison; ban handguns and implement Cullen fully.

Education and housing. Hire more teachers, repair schools, wire every school to the Internet, restore student grants, guarantee free nursery education for 3–4‑year‑olds, expand quality training. Fix the housing crisis by transferring 75% of council housing debt to unlock investment, build new social homes, and upgrade substandard stock; protect new social homes from discounted right‑to‑buy.

A nation that cares for all its places. Abolish feudal tenure; create a transparent land register; devolve Crown Estate shores and seabeds to communities. Support sustainable farming with BSE traceability, a fairer CAP, and stronger processing; reform the CFP with regional control. Double woodland cover with native species; back crofting and rural diversification. Strengthen SEPA and set national environmental targets; end nuclear reprocessing at Dounreay and pivot to renewables and decommissioning. Secure a fair North Sea settlement, add value in petro‑chemicals, end the “Great Gas Robbery,” and phase out nuclear power while expanding renewables and efficiency.

Scotland in the world. Full EU membership with a vote and a voice; modern, trade‑focused diplomacy; active UN, Commonwealth and Council of Europe roles; aid rising toward 0.7% of GDP. Build Scottish Defence Forces fit for purpose, restore historic regiments, focus on peacekeeping, remove Trident, and move out of nuclear‑based alliances while maintaining cooperation with partners.

Fully costed. A four‑year budget expands services, cuts business taxes, invests in people and infrastructure, and repays debt — funded by Scotland’s fiscal surplus, growth, and savings from wasteful programmes like Trident.

Only independence lets Scotland choose this future. Yes We Can — be free, fair and prosperous.
